newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Europe carries less airfreight in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Air France Europe carries less airfreight in 1996.

text.p: Air France Europe (formerly Air inter) said that while it carried less airfreight in 1996 it did improve cargo yields.
The airline handled 50,300 tonnes of airfreight in 1996, a decline of 11 percent on the previous year.

"The decline in tonnage is directly related to a reduction in cargo capacity, the airline having replaced Airbus 300 and 330 passenger aircraft, which could carry between seven and tonnes of freight with Airbus 320 and 319s whose bellyholds only offer between two and 2.5 tonnes," Air France Europe's marketing manager Freight, Gerard Plassat, told Reuters.

Plassat said another main factor for the reduction in cargo traffic volume last year had been the closure of a number of Air France Europe's domestic and European services in the final quarter of 1996, notably Toulon, Perpignan, Nantes, Madrid, Porto, Valencia and Malaga.

Air France Europes re-focused cargo traffic strategy - targeting small packages and express items and fewer heavy category shipments - had borne fruit in 1996 with the airline improving its yields despite a dimunition in turnover and transporting less freight, in comparision with 1995, Plassat said.

"Our 1996 turnover was down four percent on the previous year at 193 million francs but revenue per kilo increased by eight percent. Clearly, we'd like to be transporting more freight but the market niche we've cut for ourselves has produced compensating results so overall it's a satisfactory performance."
Traffic obtained from Air France Europe's door-to-door express product, Lasair, increased slightly last year with 12,200 shipments transported compared to 12,000 in 1995.
Lasair offers half-day deadlines for packages with an average weight of around 90 kilos using the airline's network of around 400 daily flights.

The performance of the French carrier's airport-to-airport and airport-to-door express product, Airporte, which has an average unit weight of 10 kilos, stagnated on 1995 levels mainly due to some major customers, such as DHL Worldwide Express, introducing their own dedicated all-cargo flights and increased competition from the integrators in general, Plassat added.
Air France Europe and Air France are to merge next April 1.
The Air France group has outlined plans to create a new parcels express division folding the two airlines activities in this sector into an integrated operation.
